item.text: {"question_id":"5B.2","answer":"The evidence supports at least one qualified economic appointment but not a consistently credible, independent, performance-based personnel system during the López Obrador period relevant to 2023. Victoria Rodríguez Ceja had economics training and more than 20 years of public-finance experience, and was nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate; this establishes qualification and a formal appointment process, but not her subsequent operational independence, performance, or retention rationale (BATCH-0039-E001). Banxico’s statutory framework provided fixed terms, qualification requirements, removal protections, and institutional autonomy, while 2022 reporting found that the bank continued unanimous rate decisions despite presidential pressure; these facts show institutional constraints and resilience, not a complete assessment of López Obrador’s 2023 empowerment of the bank (BATCH-0048-E003; BATCH-0048-E007). The administration’s early communication of respect for central-bank autonomy is pre-2023 baseline evidence and is weakened by later contrary conduct (BATCH-0004-E016). More broadly, evidence describes a governing conception that prioritized loyal, disciplined officials over technically competent administrators and used broad discretion (BATCH-0026-E006). Appointment delays and incomplete autonomous regulators materially limited institutional functioning: IFT and COFECE were left without functioning plenaries after vacancies were not filled; COFECE appointments followed a Supreme Court order, while IFT remained unresolved during the relevant reporting period (BATCH-0026-E014; BATCH-0014-E002). A wider appointment backlog also included economic and regulatory offices, with only five of 25 listed vacancies filled by the end of 2022 and additional 2023 processes pending, although appointing authority was shared with the Senate and other institutions (BATCH-0018-E015). The president also backed replacing experienced trade officials during active USMCA disputes, but the evidence does not establish whether the replacements improved outcomes or were expressly loyalty-based (BATCH-0046-E006). Overall, the record shows qualified appointments and some autonomous institutional operation alongside strong evidence of discretionary, delayed, and potentially loyalty-oriented personnel management;
